app_recommendations: Establish the universal visual doneness rule: shrimp are cooked when flesh turns opaque pink and forms a gentle 'C' curve (a tight 'O' shape indicates overcooking).
In skillet preparations, instruct users to sear shrimp first, transfer to a plate, build sauce/veggies, and re-incorporate shrimp only in the final minute to prevent tough rubbery texture.

For sheet-pan meals pairing shrimp with starchy vegetables (potatoes, squash), implement two-stage baking: roast vegetables first at 425°F for 20 minutes, then add shrimp for the final 6 minutes at 400°F.
Recommend patting shrimp thoroughly dry before searing to prevent steaming.
